item.title: Most overrated and underrated teams in Week 9 US LBM Coaches Poll
item.description: The latest US LBM Coaches Poll saw some noticeable changes following some dramatic results in Week 9 . This all helps to set the stage for the College Football Playoff selection committee's first batch of playoff rankings this week as the regular season makes the final turn down the final stretch. While we now seem to know which teams are safely in the top 12 (like Miami and Georgia), we also don't really know who else could be viable down toward the bottom of those 12 spots. Chances are a lot of two-loss teams will either be on the right side of the cut or on the outside looking in. Here are the most overrated and underrated teams in this week's coaches poll. Overrated: No. 3 Indiana When you need a miracle 60-yard kick to send a game to overtime against an unranked team, you know you're in trouble. This is the second straight week where Indiana had to struggle through a mistake-filled game, especially considering what is potentially happening in their QB room. With doubts surrounding the status of Josh Hoover, it could be backup Grant Wilson who has to take the wheel the rest of the way. Their next game against a resurgent USC could be a true test of whether this team can truly weather whatever storm is brewing in Bloomington. It's been quite some time since we've seen the Hoosiers struggle. Underrated: No. 4 Utah As of right now, Utah is only one of three unbeaten teams in the sport. And yet, they still aren't considered a top 3 team in the nation. In a potential trap game against a Cincinnati team coming off a win against Texas Tech, they took care of business, trouncing the Bearcats 49-25. Devon Damiper was excellent, throwing for 260 yards and 3 touchdowns, and the run game had over 200 yards on just 42 carries. The Utes now have two of the best wins in the entire conference. Next week? A date with BYU in the Holy War to potentially determine who represents the conference not only in the championship game, but in the CFP as well. Overrated: No. 21 Boise State As the current frontrunner for the Group of Six's lone playoff spot, the Broncos must manuever through what could turn out to be a problematic injury to QB Maddux Madsen. He left their game against Texas State with a left knee injury. True freshman Mat Cutforth had three touchdown passes, but the game was too close for comfort. Boise State can rely on having the nation's rushing leader, but they may not be able to rely on Cutforth for a prolonged period of time should Madsen be sidelined. The Group of Six CFP race just got very interesting. Underrated: No. 15 LSU If you're wondering how an idle team can be underrated, it's about who they play after their bye that should tell you. LSU may be the team that decides the entire fate of the SEC. Next week, they play Alabama at home, then host Texas. Should the Tigers go 2-0, they could become the two-loss team no one wants to face. It all rests on the shoulders of QB Sam Leavitt. If he looks like he has in the weeks leading up to the bye, LS

item.title: Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has made history by becoming the youngest title winner in the 77th year of the Formula 1 World Championship. The Italian, at 20 years and 68 days, has beaten the record of Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won the first of his four drivers' championships in 2010. Antonelli, who was still a teenager until 25 August, has secured the title in his second season in the sport. We take a look at F1's other young champions and how Antonelli's achievement compares with theirs. Kimi Antonelli First championship: 2026 Age: 20 years and 68 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 2025 Australian Grand Prix (aged 18) Antonelli has already broken a number of records on the way to becoming F1's youngest champion. In his second season, he became the youngest driver to achieve a pole position in China and the youngest to lead the championship at the next race in Japan. In Monaco, he became the youngest driver to complete a 'grand slam' of pole position, fastest lap, leading every lap and winning the race. All this after a rookie season in 2025 in which there were occasional highs but plenty of errors, and his final total of 150 points was less than half of the 319 accumulated by Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Sebastian Vettel Sebastian Vettel's four drivers' championships were won between 2010-13 [Getty Images] First championship: 2010 Age: 23 years and 133 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Third full season F1 debut: 2007 US Grand Prix (aged 19) Vettel was one of four drivers who could win the title going into the season-ending 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He was far from the best placed, though, trailing Ferrari's Fernando Alonso by 15 points before the race and his Red Bull team-mate Mark Webber by seven. The German did what he had to do by winning the grand prix and Alonso could only finish seventh, having become stuck behind the Renault of Vitaly Petrov. With Webber in eighth, Vettel won the championship by four points from Alonso. It was yet another F1 record for Vettel. He had become the youngest F1 points scorer on his debut for BMW Sauber in Indianapolis in 2007, before becoming the then youngest pole sitter and race winner at the 2008 Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso. Lewis Hamilton Lewis Hamilton won the 2008 championship by overtaking Timo Glock into the final corner of the Brazilian Grand Prix [Getty Images] First championship: 2008 Age: 23 years and 300 days Stage of his F1 career when title was won: Second full season F1 debut: 2007 Australian Grand Prix (aged 22) Lewis Hamilton's debut season in 2007 almost delivered a fairytale title but he faltered in the final two races of the year. He failed to score in China and finished seventh in Brazil, which allowed Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen to pip both Hamilton and fellow McLaren driver Fernando Alonso by a single point. Somehow the climax to the 2008 championship, also in Brazil, was even more dramatic. Hamilton

item.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion at age 20
item.description: Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his place in Formula One history as the youngest world champion. Max Verstappen took the chequered flag but all eyes were on the young Italian who takes the crown at the age of 20 years and 68 days, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel in 2010. He is the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Vanguard News The post Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion at age 20 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: When will the Golden State Valkyries parade be? Here's what to know
item.description: After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of their championship parade! The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Here's what you need to know. What time will the parade start? Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay side of the Embarcadero. The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m. Where will the parade be? The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets. If I can't watch in person, how else can I watch? Viewers can watch coverage on TV on ABC7, or stream on the free ABC7 Bay Area streaming and mobile app starting at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. Who will be there? The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win. According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade. Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said. Are there fan opportunities? Yes! Fan opportunities will include a viewing area, a championship merchandise truck, and various fan activation zones along the parade route. How will the weather be on Wednesday? < /strong> It will be partly cloudy along the bay with temperatures in the upper 60s. RELATED: Golden State Valkyries win its 1st WNBA title, beating Atlanta Dream, 68-63 Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night. Street Closures and Public Transportation Fans and workers in the area are encouraged to take public transportation such as BART and Muni due to some street closures. item.title: F1 Mexico GP: Kimi Antonelli clinches world title as Max Verstappen holds off Lewis Hamilton for victory
item.description: Motorsport photo Kimi Antonelli has written history by becoming Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion at the Mexico Grand Prix, as Red Bull's Max Verstappen beat Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to win the race. Verstappen seized control of the race during the only pitstop of the race on lap 28 of 71, leapfrogging early leader Charles Leclerc , and he fended off Leclerc's team-mate Hamilton to take victory, with Antonelli celebrating his maiden F1 title with a podium spot in third. With neither Russell nor Hamilton winning the race, Antonelli's race result was irrelevant, but he underlined his mature title winning campaign with a controlled drive as he picked off Leclerc in the second half of the race. At the start, polesitter Hamilton was challenged by Leclerc for the lead into Turn 2 and again towards Turn 4-5. Leclerc cut the grass to pass his team-mate as Hamilton lost momentum to third-placed Verstappen as well, who took advantage of the intra-team tussle to snatch second away from Hamilton. "I got pushed off by my own team-mate," Hamilton rued, as Verstappen was also angling for Leclerc to hand back the position. The Monegasque only received a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, which was deemed rather soft by both Verstappen and his own team-mate: "He's got clean air, he doesn't have to manage like the rest of us," Hamilton pointed out. In the background, the second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was punted off by slow-starting George Russell , who had dropped from second to sixth and was handed a 10-second time penalty. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing To Hamilton's point, Leclerc soon pulled out a five-second gap to second-placed Verstappen - the Dutchman only frontrunner to start on medium tyres instead of softs. Hamilton trailed by another couple of seconds ahead of the two Mercedes and the two McLaren cars. A strong start from Oscar Piastri saw him move up from a disappointing 12th grid slot to seventh, seven seconds behind the leading train. Leclerc and Verstappen both pitted on lap 28 for their only pitstop, with Leclerc moving to mediums and Verstappen switching to softs. Helped by Leclerc's additional five-second hold, Verstappen was able to jump the Ferrari in pitlane to take charge of the race, albeit on the more brittle tyre compound. "We basically need one of your magic Mexico stints," declared Verstappen's race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, as Hamilton's next-lap response by collecting mediums dropped the leading trio to fourth, fifth and sixth respectively. It handed Antonelli a brief spell in clear air at the front from Russell and Lando Norris , with Mercedes not having any real strategic options to challenge for the win - not that Antonelli would have minded one bit while on title course. item.title: ‘Firing That Was Long Overdue,’ ‘Right Move for Everyone’ — CFB World Reacts to Mike Norvell’s Departure From Florida State After Clemson Loss
item.description: CFB World Reacts to Mike Norvell’s Departure From Florida State After Clemson Loss. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida State is looking for a new head football coach, and several college football voices who weighed in Sunday backed its decision to move on from Mike Norvell. FSU President Richard McCullough told Norvell that afternoon that the school was changing the program’s leadership, effective immediately. This move came a day after a 36-24 home loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5. Rick Stockstill, an assistant on the staff and a member of the FSU Athletics Hall of Fame, was named interim head coach while the school begins a national search. The Home Loss to Clemson That Preceded Mike Norvell’s Firing Norvell’s seven-year tenure ends with a 41-39 record. Florida State went into Saturday’s game at Doak Campbell Stadium as a 5-point favorite and gave the ball away four times. Quarterback Ashton Daniels threw three interceptions and lost a fumble, and two of those picks set up 10 Clemson points in the second quarter. The Tigers stretched their lead to 29-10 before the Seminoles pulled within 29-24 on Daniels’ 41-yard touchdown pass to Jasen Lopez with 5:30 left. Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds answered with a 79-yard touchdown run, and FSU’s last drive ended in another interception. PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN’s Free CFB Playoff Predictor The defeat left Florida State 1-5 against Power Four opponents this fall and 1-4 in ACC play. Less than a day later, Norvell was out, and CFB analyst J.D. Pickell didn’t hedge on the call: “Right move for EVERYONE.” Barstool Sports affiliate Clemson Barstool pinned the timing squarely on Saturday’s result: “Clemson was really the straw that broke the camel’s back.” The loss extended a drought, too. The Seminoles haven’t beaten Clemson, Miami, or Florida since the 2023 season. Analysts Make Case That Mike Norvell’s Exit Was Overdue Other reactions looked past Saturday altogether. College football analyst Ari Wasserman needed only one line: “It had to happen.” Heisman Trophy voter Parker Thune went a step further: “A firing that was long overdue.” Norvell hit his high point only three seasons ago. His 2023 squad was 13-0 by the end of the ACC championship game, a stretch that belonged to a 19-game run of victories, the third-longest the conference has ever seen, and it landed him a fresh contract. MORE: ‘Should Be Ashamed of Themselves,’ ‘Failed as a Society’ — CFB Analysts, Fans Join Dabo Swinney in Calling Out FSU Fans’ Treatment of Mike Norvell FSU’s offense ranks No. 49 with an impact score of 78.5, and defense ranks No. 100 with an impact score of 68.6 on PFN’s Impact Rankings . Brett McMurphy, a college football insider, measured how quickly it came apart from there: “After 13-1 season in 2023, Mike Norvell was only 10-22.” The Seminoles missed bowl games in each of the previous two seasons, a stretch that included a loss to Memphis in 2024. item.title: Steelers ‘right where we want to be’ entering bye week
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers remained somewhat terse in his postgame press conference following Pittsburgh’s 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. Despite the big win over a divisional foe, Rodgers seemed reluctant to give too much praise to the Steelers offense, saying their performance was “not very complete” and that there “should’ve been a lot more points.” Still, with the Steelers now 6-2 on the season, in sole possession of first place in the AFC North, and entering a midseason bye week on a four-game winning streak, Rodgers acknowledged the team is in a good spot. “We’d like to play our best and still win. We also like to win,” he said. “We’re 6-2 going into the bye, first in the division. We’re right where we want to be.” Both Cleveland and Pittsburgh were 5-2 entering Week 8, with the Browns having already defeated the Steelers earlier in the season in a Thursday Night Football matchup at Huntington Bank Field. But back at home in Acrisure Stadium in Sunday’s rematch, the Steelers ran for 200 yards on Cleveland while only allowing 34 yards on the ground en route to a lopsided, 21-point victory. Despite the AFC North being arguably the NFL’s most competitive division in 2026 with not one team under .500, the Steelers are in the best spot of the group at midseason. The now 5-3 Browns lost in blowout fashion. The Bengals (now 5-2) won on Sunday to jump into second place in the division, but it took overtime to defeat the hapless 1-7 Titans. And the Ravens, the consensus preseason pick to win the AFC North, are now in last place at 4-4 after a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. To make matters worse for Baltimore, Lamar Jackson was injured again and is now headed to IR with an upcoming thumb injury. The Steelers’ first game after the bye will be a Sunday Night Football matchup on Nov. 15 against the Bengals in what will be another matchup between top AFC North teams. “Winning is the most important thing — 2-1 in the division now,” Rodgers said. “Either way, that game in two weeks is going to be really important.” The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier in the season. The black and gold have split their series with the Browns in 2026 but still have both matchups against the Ravens due later in the season. While the Steelers players acknowledged there’s a lot of football left to play, T.J. Watt said he’s been encouraged by how the team has found ways to win thus far. “I like that we’ve won games many different ways. We’ve come from behind. We’ve been able to hold leads. We’ve played games where we haven’t looked great. We’ve played games where we’ve looked great,” he said. “We just need to continue to grow and build off this performance … There continues to be young guys (contributing), and I think (Derrick Harmon) is coming back soon too, hopefully, so I think this bye week comes at a great time for us.” AFC North standings after Week 8 Steelers (6-2; 2-1 division) Benga

item.title: Arizona football still ranked in AP Top 25 after loss to Texas Tech
item.description: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - OCTOBER 31: Kedrick Reescano #3 of the Arizona Wildcats celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona’s loss to Texas Tech on Saturday wasn’t enough to dislodge the Wildcats from the national rankings. Arizona (6-2) is ranked No. 24 in this week’s AP Top 25, down two spots from last week. The UA received 154 points, which is a big drop from a week ago but still 60 points higher than the No. 25-ranked Florida Gators. Arizona is ranked for the third consecutive week in-season for the first time since 2023. Utah is the highest-ranked Big 12 team at No. 3 in the poll. If the Utes defeat No. 7 BYU this Saturday, they’ll come to Tucson the following Saturday with at minimum a top-three ranking. Utah could potentially move a spot or two up the rankings if it wins and Georgia loses to Ole Miss (or voters elevate Utah above a one-loss Bulldogs) or if Miami loses at Notre Dame. Interestingly, Texas Tech didn’t move up the rankings after beating the Wildcats. The Red Raiders are No. 13 in the country. Houston, which is tied with Arizona in the Big 12 standings, moved up one spot to No. 17. The USA Today Coaches poll has Arizona ranked No. 22. Arizona faces TCU on Friday night at 8:15 p.m. MST.

item.title: NFL Week 8 fan discussion
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on in the first quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills just put the finishing touches on their 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. It’s an important victory in terms of the AFC playoff race, where they hope to eventually win the AFC East and the one seed in the conference. Right now, all’s well in Bills Country. Well, enough, at least. To properly enjoy today’s win, Bills Mafia would prefer it if two of Buffalo’s biggest football enemies were handed losses. That’s right, the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots are playing late games in Week 8. The Chiefs face the Denver Broncos, while the Patriots have the Miami Dolphins. Can Denver and Miami do a favor for Buffalo? We’ll find out soon enough! If KC loses later today, the Bills will be in first place alone in the AFC. Another loss by the Patriots would further the expanse between Buffalo and New England. With that, here’s your open thread for the remainder of Sunday’s action for Week 8. That means this will serve as the open thread for Sunday Night Football, which, has yet another terrible NFC-exclusive matchup. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

item.title: Injury concerns after McKennie, De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo substitutions in Juventus 2-0 Napoli
item.description: Injury concerns after McKennie, De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo substitutions in Juventus 2-0 Napoli Napoli star Kevin De Bruyne was subbed off in an away game against Juventus with a sprained ankle, while Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Weston McKennie suffered adductor injuries. Juventus and Napoli had to make several substitutions during their meeting at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Injury updates on McKennie, De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo TURIN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Napoli’s De Bruyne and Di Lorenzo were substituted at half-time, both due to fitness problems. Sky Sport Italia reports that De Bruyne suffered a sprained ankle, while Di Lorenzo picked up an adductor injury. Gazzetta reports that Juventus midfielder McKennie also suffered an adductor injury and was replaced at half-time. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 24: Mario Hermoso of AS Roma battles for possession with Giovanni Di Lorenzo of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AS Roma at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Juventus ultimately won 2-0, with goals from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga in the second half. Both Juventus and Napoli have a tight fixture list, with two more games coming up in the next seven days. Napoli will visit Porto in the Champions League next Wednesday before hosting Lazio in Serie A next Sunday. Juventus, meanwhile, will visit AZ in the Europa League next Thursday, then travel to Fiorentina on Sunday.

item.title: Antonelli clinches maiden F1 title and becomes youngest-ever champion
item.description: Italian formula One driver Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during the Mexican Grand Prix at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. (is associated with: «Antonelli clinches maiden F1 title and becomes youngest-ever champion») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes clinched his maiden Formula One drivers' title on Sunday to become the sports' youngest-ever champion at the age of 20. He is also the first Italian to be crowned world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Antonelli sealed the title after finishing third at the Mexican Grand Prix. With four races to go, his closest challengers - team-mate George Russell and Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari - cannot catch him in the standings. Max Verstappen of Red Bull won the race in Mexico.

item.title: Live Coverage: Patriots pickup 15th turnover of the season, trail Miami
item.description: For a span of two games in five days, the New England Patriots had A.J. Brown back on the field. Sunday, when they face the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium, they will once again look to the rest of their depleted receiver corps to fill the gap as Brown sits out the game with a knee injury . How will the team fare without Brown once again? Can they stop the Miami running game? And how will the Patriots and Drake Maye handle the rainy weather in Miami? Follow along for updates from Week 8. item.title: Lincoln Riley to Stay Put After Big Ohio State Upset
item.description: Oct 11, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; USC Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley (wearing white visor) celebrates along with defensive end coach Shaun Nua after kicker Ryon Sayeri (48) hit a 54-yard field goal in the second half against the Michigan Wolverines at United Airlines Field at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum roared on Saturday night as USC handed No. 2 Ohio State a 30-18 defeat . This victory marks the biggest win for Lincoln Riley since the Trojans joined the Big Ten. The coach did not let the celebration end without making his stance clear to the public. After the standard questions were asked, Riley stepped up to the podium to read a prepared statement. He wanted to ensure he had the final word on his future with the program. Riley told the room , “I got one other thing I want to say here. I just took a second — I wanted to make sure to articulate my thoughts. This program is built on internal joy, not external applause. This win is for all the staff members, the players, the leaders, admin, all the people within the walls. I said before this game that I’m the right person for this job, and as long as all those people know that, that’s all I care about. I appreciate being a part of this university, and all it does. I appreciate our kids and our staff, and I’m going to continue to fight on because that’s what being a Trojan is all about. Adios.” This message comes after weeks of doubt regarding his tenure in Los Angeles. According to Yahoo Sports , Riley believes the win proves he can lead the team to the next level. The Path to the Playoff Before this game, USC had dropped out of the AP Top 25 following a loss to Wisconsin. A defeat to Ohio State would have killed any hope of making the College Football Playoff. Now, the Trojans can dream about a spot in the postseason. No. 4 Indiana and No. 7 UCLA are opponents they will face before the regular season comes to an end. A win against a Maryland team, which is expected to be a massive underdog, could push the team to a 10-2 record. That record might be enough to secure a berth in the Big Ten championship game and the playoff. Riley noted the difficulty of the schedule but saw the opportunity in it. He told reporters, “Again, I keep saying it, look at all the craziness across the country.” He believes that teams that hang in there and stay together will be the ones left at the end. The win over the Buckeyes was fueled by two huge plays against a defense that had been stopping everyone else. Trent Mosley scored a 69-yard touchdown on the first drive, while Mark Bowman added a 70-yard catch-and-run to set up the clinching score. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A Recruiting Pitch for the Future The victory gives Riley a stronger argument for staying another year. item.title: ‘Please Be Alright,’ ‘Completely Gut-Wrenching’ — Prayers Pour In for Jack Campbell After Lions LB’s ‘Terrifying’ Injury
item.description: ‘Please Be Alright,’ ‘Completely Gut-Wrenching’ — Prayers Pour In for Jack Campbell After Lions LB’s ‘Terrifying’ Injury The players gathered around Jack Campbell as medical personnel worked. Some knelt. Others watched with visible emotion while the Detroit Lions linebacker remained down on the Ford Field turf. Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings continued after Campbell was taken off the field, but the concern followed him. Fans and reporters sent prayers for Campbell and his family as the Lions announced he was headed to a hospital. Fans Send Prayers After Jack Campbell Is Taken to Hospital Campbell went down while tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter. Medical personnel attended to him for several minutes before he was immobilized on a backboard and taken away on a cart. “Jack Campbell is being transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury,” Lions PR announced . The update prompted an immediate response from supporters waiting for information. One fan’s message expressed the hope running through the replies. “Please be alright,” the fan wrote . “Praying with everything I have 🙏,” another fan added . “Everyone please pray🙏,” one supporter wrote . Campbell’s teammates stayed close as the medical staff prepared to move him. Detroit’s players and coaches surrounded the cart before he left the field, a scene that conveyed how worried those nearest to him were. For The Latest Information: NFL Injury Report Hawkeye Nation contributor Joe Hugen, whose connection to Iowa includes following Campbell’s former college program, described how sharply the afternoon had changed. “Completely gut wrenching… What was turning out to be a pretty great weekend soured,” Hugen wrote . He sent prayers to Campbell, adding that he was “hoping it’s extreme precautions & nothing serious or lasting.” Those were hopes for an encouraging outcome. The Lions’ initial announcement confirmed the hospital evaluation and identified the injury as involving Campbell’s neck, without providing a diagnosis or recovery timetable. That left supporters waiting for further information while sending messages directly beneath the team’s update. Praying for him,” Freeze wrote . Another supporter extended the concern to the people closest to Campbell. “This is bigger than football, sending Jack and his family all the thoughts and prayers right now!🙏,” the fan wrote . Footage of the stoppage circulated as viewers tried to understand what had happened. The clip showed the play and the response around Campbell, but it could not establish the extent of his injury. item.title: ​Week 10 college football first look: Notre Dame-Miami, BYU-Utah highlight all-time Nov. 7 schedule
item.description: ​Week 10 college football first look: Notre Dame-Miami, BYU-Utah highlight all-time Nov. 7 schedule originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's a date college football fans circled in the summer. Nov. 7 is finally here. Week 10 of the college football season is without question the best collection of games in the 2026 regular season. It comes on the heels of Tuesday's unveiling of the first College Football Playoff rankings, and there six matchups between teams in the AP Top 25. Who has the edge between No. 1 Miami and No. 4 Notre Dame in a rematch of last year's 27-24 instant classic with CFP fallout that resonates a year later? The "Holy War" is at its peak on the field between No. 3 Utah and No. 7 BYU in the Big 12. No. 2 Georgia and No. 12 Ole Miss meet in a rematch of last year's CFP quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl. No. 9 Alabama faces No. 15 LSU in Death Valley. No. 8 Kentucky faces No. 16 Tennessee, and No. 10 Texas travels to No. 19 Missouri. We're out of breath just thinking about it. Why would you do anything else but watch college football? Here is a first look at Week 10 of the college football season. Week 10 matchups between ranked teams 1. No. 1 Miami (8-0) at No. 4 Notre Dame (7-1), 7:30 p.m., NBC This will be the first top-five showdown between the Hurricanes and Irish since the legendary "Catholics vs. Convicts" game in 1988. Miami survived a 38-35 shootout with North Carolina , and Notre Dame shook off a slow start in a 35-13 victory against Navy. Quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr should put on a show in South Bend, and the matchup on the perimeter with Miami receiver Malachi Toney and Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is must-see TV. When nostalgia collides with the present tense in this fashion, special things happen. 2. No. 7 BYU (7-1) at No. 3 Utah (8-0), 12 p.m., ABC It's the first top-10 showdown between the Cougars and Utes and just the fifth matchup where both teams are ranked. The teams split the previous four ranked matchups. Utah has the inside draw at the Big 12 championship game, and the Cougars need this one without the benefit of Texas Tech on the schedule. BYU has won the last three meetings. 3. No. 2 Georgia (7-1) at No. 12 Ole Miss (6-2), 7:30 p.m., ABC The Rebels have won two of the last three meetings against Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss averaged 340.5 total yards with five TDs and no interceptions in two meetings against the Bulldogs last season. Can he put Ole Miss on his back in a must-win situation against a Georgia defense that recalibrated in a 27-8 victory against Florida? It's part of another loaded SEC schedule. MORE: Why Georgia can be trusted among the contenders 4. No. 9 Alabama (6-2) at No. 15 LSU (6-2), 3:30 p.m., ABC Is this an elimination game in the CFP playoff race? item.title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals: 4 losers and 3 winners from the game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys returned home looking to show they could grind out back-to-back wins after last week’s dismantling of the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas’ defense played with considerably more physicality and creating turnovers until the late game disappointment. Offensively, a couple of unlikely names provided important moments, although the running game and self-inflicted mistakes caused a massive fourth quarter collapse, eventually losing 33-30 in overtime. We have four losers and three winners from the game, but the damage done to the season is absolutely the biggest loser. Loser: Cowboys running game One week after Javonte Williams ran wild against Philadelphia, Dallas wasn’t able to reproduce anything close to it, and against this Arizona defense that’s most frustrating. Williams totalled 56 yards on 24 carries, averaging only 2.3 yards per attempt, while Tyler Goodson had 14 yards on seven carries, easy maths there on yards per carry. Arizona consistently won around the line of scrimmage and Dallas struggled badly in short-yardage situations. When Dallas was leading in the fourth quarter, that was exactly when the Cowboys should have been able to lean on their running game and drain the clock. Instead, Prescott had to continue carrying too much of the offensive responsibility, which made hard work closing the game out and gave Arizona the chances it needed to get the win. Loser: Cowboys defense versus Tyler Allgeier This one is difficult to explain. Tyler Allgeier entered Sunday with just 176 rushing yards on 61 carries this season, averaging only 2.9 yards per attempt. Against Dallas, he explodeded for 128 yards on only six carries, and he was the third running back on their depth chart. The biggest damage came on a 63-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter that suddenly turned a comfortable 17-3 Dallas lead into a one-score game. Allgeier then hurt the Cowboys again through the air, catching a five-yard touchdown from Gardner Minshew in the fourth quarter to make it 24-17. That meant a player averaging fewer than three yards per carry coming into the game suddenly became Arizona’s biggest offensive weapon. The Dallas defense gave up 128 rushing yards on six attempts, that’s more than 21 yards per carry, to a backup running back and that is simply unacceptable. Loser: Rashan Gary There are bad penalties, then there are penalties like Gary did. Arizona faced third-and-10 from the Dallas 29 with 2:23 remaining and Dallas leading 27-17. Gardner Minshew’s pass fell incomplete. The Cowboys should have been walking off the field with Arizona facing fourth down. Instead, Gary was called for roughing the passer, 15 yards and an automatic first down. On the very next snap, Minshew found Trey McBride for a 14-yard touchdown, suddenly making it 27-24. It was an terrible penalty at one of the worst possible moments that helped cost the team the game. Loser: Brian Scho

item.title: Antonelli seals historic maiden F1 title with podium finish in Mexican GP
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has become a Formula 1 world champion for the first time in his Formula 1 career. Antonelli finished on the podium in the Mexico City Grand Prix . The young Italian is the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, taking the record from Sebastian Vettel. Antonelli secured the final spot on the podium at the Mexican Grand Prix , finishing third behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. The Italian delivered a composed performance despite the numerous interruptions and Safety Car periods, maintaining his position in the closing stages to secure the result he needed to become Formula 1 world champion. Antonelli is only in his second season in Formula 1 this year. The Mercedes driver is just 20 years and 68 days old at the moment he clinches the title. That makes him younger than Vettel, who was 23 years, 4 months and 11 days old when he won his first world title. It has been a remarkable season for Antonelli. After a difficult debut year with Mercedes last season, he has been incredibly dominant this year. The Italian has adapted brilliantly to the new generation of cars and has been dominant and near the front of the field in almost every race weekend. Antonelli on the podium in almost every F1 race The Italian has finished on the Formula 1 podium in almost every race this year. By the Mexico City Grand Prix, he had claimed 15 podiums in 18 races, nine of them victories. By comparison, teammate George Russell had won three times and secured nine podiums in 18 races. Antonelli missed the podium only in Barcelona, Silverstone and Baku. He suffered mechanical trouble in Barcelona. In Silverstone, a run of bad luck saw him finish in fifteenth place. In Baku, he had a difficult qualifying session and crashed. He hit the barriers in Q1, forcing him to fight his way through the field from sixteenth on the grid. A historic year in Formula 1 for Antonelli It was clear from the start of the year that Mercedes had a strong car. George Russell won the first race. In the races that followed, Antonelli showed that he had what it takes to become champion. The Italian won in China, Japan and Miami. Antonelli then won in Canada and claimed another victory in Monaco the following race weekend. Antonelli has enjoyed a remarkable year in Formula 1. Photo: Red Bull Contentpool Antonelli has enjoyed a remarkable year in Formula 1. Photo: Red Bull Contentpool After Monaco, Antonelli went three races without a win. He returned to the top step of the podium at Spa-Francorchamps. It was a little while longer before he could do so again. Norris proved too strong in Hungary and Zandvoort. Antonelli's triumph at his home race in Monza Antonelli's most memorable victory, perhaps, came at his home race. In Monza, a grid penalty meant he had to start from the back of the field. He produced a phenomenal charge through the field to take the win. A week later, he also won in Madrid. After failing to win in Baku, Malaysia and Singapore, he had the chanc

item.title: Paul McGinley suggests whether he thinks Ian Poulter or Lee Westwood will ever be Ryder Cup captains
item.description: Photo by Ross Kinnaird/Getty Images Paul McGinley has revealed the reason that he does not expect to see Ian Poulter or Lee Westwood become Ryder Cup captains in the future following their moves to LIV Golf. The European Ryder Cup team had a long list of captains waiting in the wings heading into the 2023 event in Rome, with the likes of Westwood, Poulter, Sergio Garcia, and Graeme McDowell likely to follow Henrik Stenson. However, Stenson was stripped of the captaincy after deciding to follow the quartet to LIV Golf in 2022. Westwood, Poulter, and Garcia all resigned their memberships with the DP World Tour at various stages. Both Poulter and Garcia have confirmed that they are leaving LIV Golf ahead of the 2027 season. However, that does not mean that they are back in the frame to succeed Luke Donald after Adare Manor next September. Paul McGinley casts doubt on Ian Poulter or Lee Westwood ever being Ryder Cup captain In 2017, the European Tour introduced a new rule that banned players who decline membership from ever being Ryder Cup captain. Of course, that rule came in several years before LIV turned the game upside down. Nevertheless, speaking to The Times , Paul McGinley believes that the rules are unlikely to change to accommodate those coming back from LIV. “ Ian Poulter , it’s going to be the biggest regret of his life that he never became Ryder Cup captain. The same for Lee Westwood ,” he said. “Well, I see no enthusiasm from the players’ committee to have the regulation that excludes them lifted. So in that sense, yes, I think the boat [Ryder Cup captaincy] has sailed.” McGinley criticises those who left the DP World Tour for LIV Golf over their conduct Ever since Brooks Koepka made the decision to leave LIV Golf towards the end of 2025, there has been plenty of debate regarding how any returning players should be treated by the PGA Tour and the DP World Tour. Obviously, that conversation is much more prevalent now that several players have decided to leave LIV. McGinley was asked whether that punishment of never being able to captain the Ryder Cup team is too severe. But the victorious skipper from 2014 insisted that those players made their bed with how they handled joining LIV in the first place. “I understand why they went to LIV and I think if I’d been in their position, I might have done the same. In my view, going was not the biggest mistake. Their short-sightedness, in being critical of the DP World Tour as they departed, this was the problem. They burned their bridges as they crossed to the other side and a lot of people were offended by that. Half of the team I captained in the Ryder Cup at Gleneagles went to LIV. Half of them. Not one of them showed any graciousness to the Tour they were leaving. That broke my heart,” he said. “They’re now trying to be more conciliatory. ‘Coming back to my home’ is what Sergio wrote recently, but people remember what was said four years ago. Back then, if these guys had been getting good adv

item.title: Bruno Fernandes: Persistent admirers planning to submit mega offer for Man United talisman in January
item.description: Bruno Fernandes: Persistent admirers planning to submit mega offer for Man United talisman in January Manchester United are gearing up for a pivotal January window, with fans waiting with bated breath to see if INEOS will provide funds to strengthen an underperforming squad. It is clear that the team needs new defenders, both at the heart of the backline and at left-back, as well as a striker amid Benjamin Sesko’s injury woes. Given United’s co-owners’ penny-pinching nature, not too many funds might be allocated in the winter, barring major player sales. Lisandro Martinez is one player whose form and temperament may dictate a parting of ways once the transfer window opens, amid interest from several clubs . Bruno Fernandes: Time up? Another superstar who could make way is Bruno Fernandes. This was unthinkable a couple of months ago when he was named the PFA Player of the Year after his record-breaking previous campaign. However, amid United’s poor form and a public spat with head coach Michael Carrick, INEOS could look to get rid should the right offer present itself. The Portuguese ace has since patched up with the former United midfield legend, but his on-field performances have not been up to scratch. Nevertheless, that has not stopped teams from showing interest, with Saudi Pro League sides among the club captain ‘s most persistent admirers. Al-Hilal to return for Bruno Fernandes TMW have reported that Al-Hilal could return for the 32-year-old in the winter. His current deal ends next summer and talks over a new long-term deal have since stalled . But the Red Devils do hold the option of triggering a one-year extension. The Saudi side are prepared to pay £46 million to get the deal done, a far cry from the £100 million they were ready to spend a couple of summers ago. “Al Hilal are ready to make a bid to snatch Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes as early as January. Will INEOS accept? “The Saudi club is considering a significant offer, with rumors circulating as high as €55 million.” Such a bid might not be enough to tempt INEOS into a sale mid-season, but it will be intriguing to see if any club bids high enough in the coming windows. item.title: 11 winners, 8 losers from Detroit Lions’ win over the Minnesota Vikings
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Jahmyr Gibbs #0 of the Detroit Lions reacts during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images One week after a stressful NFC North divisional tilt, the Detroit Lions were faced with a similar situation. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings came to town boasting a historically dominant defense led by a coordinator that had given Detroit fits over the years. Despite the pressure on- and off-the-field, the Lions kicked off November with a win and gave Minnesota their first taste of losing. The game as a whole wound up being overshadowed by a disturbing injury to star linebacker Jack Campbell . Players put their bodies on the line to win football games, yet freak incidents like these highlight why these athletes are people first and foremost. Jared Goff said it best: Jared Goff says the Jack Campbell injury was a dose of reality. You remember in those moments that he's a husband and a father. — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) November 1, 2026 Although Detroit walked away with a win today, the team had to weather a scary circumstance to the heart and soul of their team. For the sake of analysis, I will delve into “Winners” and “Losers”, but we need to remember that in the grand scheme of things, they do more for this franchise and fanbase than just play football. Note: The label of “loser” is used to evaluate and contrast in-game performance and is not an indictment of a player’s ability, value, or character. The term is not intended to be disrespectful in nature. Winner: Drew Petzing, OC Football is a chess match of player versus player and, more importantly, coach versus coach. The key matchup in this game was Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing versus Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores. For Petzing, he boasted one of most potent offenses entering the week. For Flores, his defense had singlehandedly carried the Vikings to an undefeated record. The outcome of this heavyweight tilt was arguably a split decision win for Petzing. Flores landed his fair share of punches (four sacks and a below-average passing day from the Lions offense), but it was a darn good fight from Petzing. Best of all, it showed resilience and adaptability. After the first half, I was ready to crown Petzing as a loser, but the halftime adjustments worked wonders. In the first half, the Lions tried to run too many plays horizontal to the line of scrimmage. The Vikings capitalized, often tackling the Lions players for losses. The Lions only ran a few deep shots (mainly a 46-yarder to Jameson Williams) because there was rarely time for downfield routes to develop. In the second half, the tune changed. Instead of running east-west, Jahmyr Gibbs broke free on a north-south carry and sprinted for a 30-yard touchdown. item.title: Five quick takeaways from historic Mexico GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Antonelli celebrates in style with mature podium drive What a luxury to enjoy your coronation with so little pressure. Kimi Antonelli did admit to being extra tense this weekend as his maiden world championship loomed, but all he had to do was keep it on the island to cruise to the finish line. Antonelli didn't have his finest qualifying session in Mexico, but from fifth on the grid he benefitted from Russell's slow start to get ahead and shadow the leaders. With neither Russell nor Hamilton winning the race, Antonelli didn't even have to finish the race. And as virtually all of his top team rivals got their elbows out, Antonelli drove a mature and low-key race - the only bit of excitement coming when he made a lunge on Charles Leclerc to grab third after the red flag. That move ensured he would celebrate his maiden title on Mexico's famous podium fronting an electric Foro Sol stadium. On a weekend Mercedes didn't have the upper hand, it was a worthy way to write a fresh chapter of F1 history. - Fil Cleeren Leclerc vs Hamilton incident costs Ferrari win Ferrari was ideally positioned to claim its third victory of the season in Mexico. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were first and third on the grid, and front-row starter George Russell dropped like a stone in the second phase of the start. The red cars went wheel to wheel in the first section of corners, with Hamilton narrowly retaining the lead out of Turn 3, but when Leclerc launched a move around the outside in Turn 4, both of them ended up going off track, with the Monegasque cutting the corner. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton lost momentum and was passed by Verstappen; Leclerc got a five-second penalty – more lenient than the regular 10 seconds due to mitigating circumstances, the stewards explained – but that wasn’t enough to hold Verstappen off in the pitlane. The Monegasque went on to lose two more spots at the second start – after the race was red-flagged for Valtteri Bottas ’ crash – and flat-spotted his tyres in the process. Let’s put it plainly: this race could have been a Ferrari 1-2, and under the chequered flag it was a 2-4, because its drivers couldn’t behave. And Hamilton insistently calling for a harsher penalty for his team-mate likely wasn’t quite what Fred Vasseur wanted to see either. - Ben Vinel Verstappen's latest win proves Red Bull is back Kimi Antonelli is a lucky boy that Red Bull's start to the season wasn't great - and Max Verstappen lost too much ground early on to realistically remain in the championship fight. Because had he stayed within striking distance, there would be a lot more for the Italian to worry about this year. Instead, what we're seeing now isn't a comeback in the championship sense - but it's still a demonstration of what a force Verstappen can be. As soon as Red Bull gave him a car good enough to fight at the front, he started making the most of it. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bul

item.title: Kimi Antonelli Beats Vettel to Become F1’s Youngest Champion: Facts and Records
item.description: Andrea Kimi Antonelli is the 2026 F1 world champion after the Mexico GP, becoming the youngest title winner ever at 20 years, 68 days in only his second season. Mercedes ’ Antonelli had his first shot at the title in Austin and sealed it in this weekend’s F1 Mexico GP by finishing third. He arrived in Mexico with 365 points, 123 clear of teammate George Russell and 124 clear of Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who both had only an outside chance. It has been a dominant season, with Antonelli adjusting well to the new car and regulations. Going into Mexico, he had 9 wins from 18 Grands Prix, 15 podiums and 7 poles, including five wins in a row from China to Monaco. Russell started well by winning the season opener, but three retirements hurt his challenge. Antonelli is now the 36th driver to be crowned Formula 1 champion, and only the third from Italy after Giuseppe Farina and Alberto Ascari. The country waited 73 years for another one. GRANDE KIMI!! item.title: The secrets behind Kimi Antonelli’s historic F1 triumph – and how Ferrari missed out on Italian superstar
item.description: It probably wasn’t quite how Kimi Antonelli envisaged his inaugural top-of-the-step moment. “Congratulations… Kimi Raikkonen!” bellowed long-time Formula 1 podium announcer Bob Constanduros, as the young Italian jumped onto the podium at the Shanghai International Circuit in March. Antonelli, lad with a ruthless cutting edge intertwined with a feverishly boyish charm, gestured and laughed with his team down below. While it was a comical blunder, comparisons to his namesake Finnish driver (sadly for this section, Antonelli’s middle name was not in tribute to Raikkonen) seem somewhat appropriate for the 20-year-old Italian who, on Sunday night, became the youngest Formula 1 world champion ever. Raikkonen, Ferrari ’s last champion in 2007, was known as “The Iceman”, such was his cold, unflustered demeanour. And in just his second F1 season, Antonelli’s poise and serenity have been his biggest asset amid the season of his life. Antonelli’s third-place finish in Mexico, off the back of his brilliant lights-to-flag victory in Austin last week, rather epitomised the Italian’s near-flawless campaign – and that of his forlorn Mercedes teammate, George Russell . While Antonelli made ground at the start in Mexico City, Russell dropped back and received a 10-second penalty after spinning Isack Hadjar. It rather summed up the forlorn Briton’s year. Antonelli has not just beaten teammate George Russell this season but wiped the floor with him this year (Getty) A season which had Russell as the clear pre-season favourite – in the quickest car on the grid – has resulted in Toto Wolff ’s Italian protege, the teen he trusted with filling Lewis Hamilton ’s seismic boots, dominating the 2026 campaign. And for Antonelli, it is a history-making achievement. At 20 years and 68 days, the Italian becomes the sport’s youngest-ever champion in its 76-year history, beating Sebastian Vettel’s previous record at 23 years of age. In quite the twist of fate, Antonelli was actually born on the same day that Vettel made his F1 race weekend debut in Turkey in August 2006. Astonishingly, Antonelli also becomes Italy’s first world champion in 73 years, when the great Alberto Ascari won for Ferrari in 1963. Alongside multiple Grand Slam champion Jannik Sinner, he is now Italian sport’s biggest star. His maturity, a year on from being in tears at Spa-Francorchamps after a disastrous qualifying performance, has been startlingly impressive, witnessed too by journalists up and down the paddock. At the season-opener in Australia, The Independent was present as Mercedes held a media event early on the first media day morning: the ultimate indication that a team is confident in their new car. Typically with such events, there was a preamble before the driver Q&A: coffees, biscuits, small talk. Antonelli swooped over, shook every reporter’s hand and asked how their journey down under was, such was the Middle East travel chaos that had ensued days before. item.title: AI-Generated Photos: We Are Already Cleaning Up Our Register – INEC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has commenced the process of cleaning up its preliminary Register of Voters following the identification of records with suspected AI-generated photographs and other irregularities. The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, said on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics that its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) had flagged 268 records for review. “What we are currently doing now is looking at all these 268 records that ABIS already flagged as AI-generated or even something of irregularities,” he said. Bayode explained that some people allegedly used their official credentials to create questionable profiles, exploiting a registration option designed for persons with disabilities who do not have complete fingers or have no fingers. According to him, the option, known as special registration, was used to deceive the system and was among the irregularities detected by ABIS. He said the commission had begun cleaning up the affected records. “Those that we have seen, we are cleaning up,” Bayode said. Bayode Lawrence However, he clarified that not every photograph enhanced with artificial intelligence would be removed, distinguishing between images generated entirely by AI and genuine photographs improved with AI tools on mobile phones. “Those that we know it is the AI on the phone that helped enhance their pictures, we can’t exclude such people because it was the AI on the phone that does that. Such people will still be on the register but those AI-generated, those photographs, all these will be removed. We are already looking at them,” he said. The controversy followed the publication of INEC’s preliminary Register of Voters online on October 26, after screenshots circulated on social media showing questionable photographs attached to voter records, including entries from parts of Edo State. The concerns also included allegations of duplicate entries and reports that names of deceased persons appeared on the register. In response, INEC said the online version was the same preliminary register displayed physically at Registration Areas nationwide from October 9 to 15. It explained that the publication did not reflect all the data-cleanup activities already in progress. The commission also said the register was not yet the final certified version and that the display, claims and objections exercise was designed to allow members of the public to identify inaccuracies and questionable entries before certification. INEC has said it will complete the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026. item.title: CAF picks Nigeria’s Samson Adamu as new General Secretary
item.description: Nigerian Samson Adamu has been appointed the new General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF). CAF announced the appointment on Sunday, on its website following a comprehensive recruitment process conducted by the continental football governing body. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that Adamu had been serving as acting General Secretary since March, following the resignation of Veron Mosengo-Omba. Mosengo-Omba subsequently became president of the football federation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). CAF President, Patrice Motsepe, was quoted in the statement on its website as saying that the appointment followed a competitive recruitment exercise, during which the position was widely advertised and several candidates interviewed. Adamu has worked with CAF for eight years, serving first as Director of Competitions and later as Director of Tournaments and Events. “Adamu brings extensive experience in African football administration, having joined CAF in 2018 as Director of Competitions before subsequently serving as Director of Tournaments and Events. “He has played a leading role in the delivery of several major continental competitions, including CAF’s flagship tournament, the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations,” Motsepe was quoted as saying. A graduate of the FIFA Master programme in International Management, Law and Humanities of Sport, Adamu brings considerable institutional knowledge and experience to his new role. NAN reports that Adamu is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration and support the implementation of its strategic priorities. He is the son of Amos Adamu, a former Director of Sports in the then Ministry of Sports and a former FIFA Executive Committee member. The appointment places Adamu among a distinguished line of CAF General Secretaries, including members of Egypt’s Fahmy family. Mourad Fahmy served from 1961 to 1982, followed by his son, Mustapha Fahmy, from 1982 to 2010, and grandson, Amr Fahmy, who held the position from 2017 to 2019. The post CAF picks Nigeria’s Samson Adamu as new General Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos sail into semi finals, to meet Brazil
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos booked their place in the semi-finals of this year’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup finals after securing a 1-0 victory over Venezuela on Sunday night, with Azeezatt Oduntan scoring a late penalty in the 89th minute. The quarter-final contest had been closely fought, with Nigeria creating several opportunities but finding Venezuela goalkeeper Valeria Rebanales a huge stumbling block. The Flamingos enjoyed much of the attacking play in the first half, but Rebanales produced a couple of saves to keep the scores level. Midfielder Favour Nkwocha was also cautioned as Nigeria continued to press for an opening goal. Head Coach Hakeem Busari made his first change of the evening, introducing Precious Oscar for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi as Nigeria looked to find a way through. The deadlock remained unbroken until the 88th minute, when the referee initially awarded Nigeria a penalty before being invited to the VAR monitor to review the decision. Following the review, the penalty was upheld, and Oduntan stepped forward to convert from the spot with a minute left on the clock, giving Nigeria the breakthrough. Top scorer Oluebube Umejiaku had won the penalty for the Flamingos, setting up Oduntan to deliver the decisive moment of the contest. The victory sends Nigeria into the semi-finals, where they will face Brazil, who secured a 2-1 win over China in their quarter-final encounter. item.title: Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel artist to hit one billion YouTube views
item.description: Nigerian gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has surpassed one billion views on YouTube, becoming the first African gospel artist to achieve the milestone. Bassey’s official YouTube channel, Nathaniel Bassey Main, has amassed more than 1.014 billion views and 5.24 million subscribers since its creation in 2011, according to figures displayed on the platform at the time of filing this report. The achievement coincides with the October 2026 edition of the Hallelujah Challenge, the online prayer and worship programme founded by the gospel minister in 2017. The monthly initiative features midnight sessions of praise, worship and prayers, attracting participants from different parts of the world. Initially launched as an online worship gathering, the Hallelujah Challenge has grown into an international Christian movement, with thousands of people participating in its live sessions and millions more watching recorded editions. Bassey is known for popular gospel songs such as Imela , Onise Iyanu , Olowogbogboro and You Are God , which have contributed to his popularity among gospel music audiences in Nigeria and beyond. The one-billion-view milestone has generated excitement among his followers, with some suggesting that the minister could explore opportunities to monetise the growing audience of his online worship sessions. However, Bassey has maintained that the Hallelujah Challenge is primarily focused on worship and spiritual devotion rather than revenue generation. item.title: Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list
item.description: …Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action By Anayo Okoli The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent. The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation. Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council. In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition. The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation. “The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests. “We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said. The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties. It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good. While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests. “We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said. The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added. The post Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Stop opposition politics, integrate with FG, Soludo tells South-East leaders
item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government. Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka. The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party. The governor said that the coalition of political parties in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election represented a new direction for the region’s political engagement. According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre. He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president. He argued that the 5,000 votes Tinubu received in Anambra in the 2023 presidential election had contributed to attracting significant projects to the state and the region. “If 5,000 votes could attract these projects to our state and the region, imagine what would happen if we mobilised the electorate to give him massive support,” he said. On the economic reforms of the government, Soludo acknowledged efforts to stabilise foreign exchange availability and address fiscal challenges, noting that, although progress had been made, more work was required. He called for structural realignment of the coalition, saying existing campaign and mobilisation structures would be streamlined during the week. The governor urged grassroots mobilisers to adopt door-to-door campaigns, drawing lessons from successful political mobilisation strategies used during the 1983 elections. He also advised campaign teams not to be distracted by opposition criticism and verbal attacks on social media, but to remain focused on communicating what he described as the truth. Soludo reaffirmed his commitment to long-term governance, saying that the decisions being taken by his administration were aimed at securing a prosperous future for generations to come. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Mr Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as a landmark in the political history of Anambra. Ezeokenwa said that the coalition was an unprecedented political alignment involving different parties united in support of Tinubu’s re-election. He commended Soludo for providing leadership and facilitating the alliance, assuring that APGA would fully support the governor’s political direction. “Our party structure is ready to execute the instructions and deliver results at the polls,” he said. Also speaking, APC Chairman in Anambra, Sen. Emma Anosike, expressed appreciation for the development strides in the state. Anosike said that the political realignment was aimed at positioning Anambra more directly within the government’s political and developmental framework. He called for

item.title: 2027: Otti warns supporters against disrupting opposition campaigns
item.description: Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights. Otti said anyone found obstructing rival political parties from holding lawful rallies or other campaign activities would face arrest, irrespective of party affiliation. The governor gave the warning on Sunday in Umuahia while flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he stressed that political competition must be conducted within the confines of the law. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said. Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed. He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. He urged opposition parties to examine available performance data before making claims about the state, citing its ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations. “You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. item.title: NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal
item.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term. Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President. Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years. Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges. He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty. “While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years. “He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said. He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living. “What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected. “Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said. The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion. He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership. The post NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Akpabio predicts highest South-South votes for Tinubu from Akwa Ibom
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election. Akpabio made the declaration on Sunday during a special church service at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, organised to dedicate the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 election campaigns to God. The service had the theme, “We Are Well Able”. In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, the Senate President said Akwa Ibom indigenes, particularly APC members, must close ranks and present a united front to ensure the party’s success at the polls. He said the state had a responsibility to reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given him by mobilising votes for the President. According to him, the support of Tinubu contributed to his emergence as Senate President, making him the number three citizen in the country. “Whether you like him or not, he is there today. The only way to thank Mr President for that support is to give him all our votes. “From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said. In an address titled, “One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God”, Akpabio said while the people acknowledged God’s sovereignty over their individual and collective destinies, they must also uphold righteousness, justice and mercy. He described Akwa Ibom as a Nigerian success story, attributing its progress to purposeful leadership, peace and development. The Senate President said development should not be measured only by roads and buildings but also by the bridges built between people and the hope restored in their lives. He urged political leaders and party members to sustain the state’s progress and ensure that its future achievements surpassed those already recorded. On party unity, Akpabio cautioned against divisions between old and new members of the APC, insisting that all members should be treated equally. “In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility,” he said. Using a biblical reference from John 14:2, he said there was room for everyone in the party, regardless of when they joined or their political standing. He added that political ambitions should not override the welfare of the people, urging party members to conduct their campaigns in ways that respect human dignity. Akpabio further said the development of Akwa Ibom was inseparable from the progress of Nigeria, stressing that the state could not remain indifferent to insecurity and hardship in other parts of the country. “Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom c
